stats.name: h1_dominance_P1_over_P2
stats.null_model: amplitude-adjusted Fourier-transform surrogates of the same recording (same power spectrum, same amplitude distribution)

controls.description: a periodic physiological signal must give a dominant H1 loop under delay embedding (dominance >= 5)
POST-HOC sensitivity sweep over 9 settings (3 window lengths x band-pass on/off, plus 3 SW1PerS sliding-window dimensions): is the pre-stated outcome one unlucky choice?
controls.detail: best dominance over the 9 settings is 2.086; pre-stated setting gives 1.157

controls.description: AAFT surrogates keep the spectrum and the amplitudes but destroy the deterministic cycle

findings.claim: MIT-BIH 100 (normal sinus rhythm (69 M)): delay embedding (m=3, tau=72 samples at 360 Hz) gives H1 dominance 1.16 against a median 1.25 over 200 AAFT surrogates (p 0.5572). Pre-stated criteria: NOT MET.
findings.caveat: one 20 s window of one lead of one recording; tau is chosen from the recording's own dominant spectral frequency, which the surrogates share. A post-hoc sweep over 9 further settings reaches at best dominance 2.09, so the outcome is not one unlucky parameter choice.
